seam: The audit engine's static rule contract (StaticRule, the static registry, the parsed-markup substrate) and its tier map
prompt: Add a static cairn-audit rule named `img-alt` that flags an `` element in a component when the element has no `alt` attribute at all. An empty `alt=""` marks a decorative image on purpose and must pass, and a bound `alt={...}` counts as present. A missing alt is an accessibility failure, so the rule should fail the audit run, not just warn. Its message should tell the author what to add and why. Give it a test. It's done when the repo's gates for a new audit rule pass.

expectations: A new module under src/lib/audit/rules/static exports a StaticRule with id 'img-alt' and tier 'error', and staticRules() registers it.
The check walks each parsed component's nodes for a RegularElement named img and reads its attributes, flagging one with no attribute named alt; alt="" and alt={expr} both pass.
Each finding carries the node's file, line, start, and end, and a message that names the fix (add alt text, or alt="" for a decorative image) and why.
A unit test under src/tests/unit/audit covers the missing, empty, and bound cases, and the registry membership test in run.test.ts lists the new id.

The tier map in skills/cairn-admin-screens/SKILL.md lists img-alt under the static error tier, the reference page's static-rules table gains a row, and CHANGELOG.md's ## Unreleased section gains an entry.
The audit unit tests, check:package, check:comments, and the type check pass.

checks.source: the bound-alt case the prompt names; no audit test carries such a fixture at either ref (alt="" already appears in rulings.chip-ground-collision.test.ts, so it cannot be the check)

judge.text: The rule finds images by walking the parsed component nodes (a RegularElement named img and its attributes list) rather than matching a regular expression over the raw source text.
The rule's test proves all three cases: an img with no alt attribute is flagged, an img with alt="" is not, and an img with a bound alt={...} is not.

The rule is registered at error tier in staticRules(), and both the registry membership test in run.test.ts and the tier map the tree's check:package gate reads list `img-alt` under the static error tier.
Each finding's message tells the author to add alt text describing the image, or alt="" when the image is decorative, and says why (assistive technology has nothing to announce otherwise).
